runs.text:
According to the fundamental equations of the Big Bang, you shouldn't exist. The early universe should have created equal amounts of matter and antimatter, which would have immediately annihilated on contact, leaving a cosmos filled with nothing but pure, empty light.

To explain why our half of the universe survived, physicists hoped for an elegant, reality-breaking loophole: what if antimatter experiences gravity as a repulsive force? If antimatter "falls up," the two halves of the early universe would have simply pushed each other away before they could finish burning.
